vpnRules.intro: Traffic control between VPN networks (FORWARD chain)

empty.title: VPN Inter-Network Rules
empty.subtitle: Define how traffic flows between VPN networks
empty.whatBody: VPN rules control the server's FORWARD chain. These rules determine whether traffic can pass between different VPN networks. Since all VPN traffic flows through the server, these rules provide complete control over inter-network communication.
empty.allow1: Access admin panel from office network
empty.allow2: Allow specific nodes to reach other networks
empty.howBody: All VPN traffic flows through the server. VPN rules are applied on the server and determine which traffic can be forwarded.
empty.noteBody: When you create a VPN rule, the source node's AllowedIPs configuration is automatically updated. However, existing connected devices may need to reload their configuration.

matrix.title: Network policies
matrix.help: Rows are the source network, columns the destination. Partial: some ports, protocols or hosts are treated differently. Click a cell to add a rule for that pair.
matrix.helpNft: Without a rule, networks are isolated from each other.
matrix.helpIptables: In iptables mode VPN traffic is accepted unless a rule drops it.

reason.iptables_default: default (iptables mode accepts VPN traffic no rule drops)
